change.summary: The entire Sync REST surface on preview.twilio.com was retired — 18 path templates, all methods. Twilio's wording: 'any requests sent to this endpoint will result in a 400 error.' Migration is a host swap: the same paths exist on sync.twilio.com/v1.

spec.note: Ten days LATE. The spec was regenerated after the shutoff, so for ten days Twilio's published OpenAPI advertised endpoints that were already returning 400. Verified by cloning the repo: the diff has exactly 18 removed /Sync/ path lines and zero added. A spec-watcher would have been told after its users were already broken.

changelog.note: 60 days of notice, the cleanest announcement in the dataset. But note the SDK changelogs lie by omission: CHANGES.md in the very commit that deleted 18 paths does not mention Sync at all, listing only unrelated Flex and Messaging entries.

sdk.note: The earliest public signal of any kind: 'chore: remove preview sync api', two and a half months before the changelog post. Not an announcement — an artifact. It is also unreliable on its own, because autogeneration re-added the code twice afterwards before the final deletion.

contract.note: The only case in the dataset that fails loudly, with a 400. Recorded as detected on the stated EOL date, though no post-shutoff source was found proving the endpoint actually started returning 400 that day.

notes: effective_at is Twilio's stated date, not an observed one — no wire-level complaint about a 400 from preview.twilio.com/sync was found anywhere. The verified damage was collateral and much larger than the retirement itself: the codegen run deleted twilio/rest/preview/sync/ but left its import in preview/__init__.py, so `import twilio.rest` raised ModuleNotFoundError for EVERY twilio-python user across six releases (9.5.1 to 9.6.4, 2025-03-20 to 2025-07-10). An outside contributor found and fixed it in one line. Verified per tag by checking both the import line and the package's existence.
